category: result used before its stated criterion / misleading reference semantics
dependency_chain: The Poisson-thinning proof factors P(M=j,K=k) at 113-115 and concludes independence by "the discrete criterion (Theorem ref thm:indep-criterion)" at 119-121. That labelled theorem is not introduced until 338-345 later in the same lecture. The actual earlier available criterion is the discrete definition in Lecture 4 at 262-266, but it is not the cited target.
independent_analysis: The factorization at 113-115 does establish the Lecture-4 point-mass independence criterion, so the conclusion is mathematically sound. It is nevertheless a forward use of a not-yet-defined labelled theorem in the pedagogical dependency graph; the reader must either infer an unstated criterion or jump ahead. Relinking the sentence to the Lecture-4 definition, or moving/introducing the criterion before the proof, makes the proof's prerequisite explicit.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_07_math review independently checked the joint-law section; this finding is based on the source order and resolved label graph.

category: appendix drops independence and nondegeneracy hypotheses for limit theorems
dependency_chain: The formula appendix gives WLLN/SLLN and CLT solely as formulas for S_n at 356-360. The source theorems require an iid sequence: Lecture 10:318-324 and 359-365. Lecture 11:19-25 also requires iid input and standardizes by sigma.
independent_analysis: Finite variance alone cannot justify either displayed limit. Let X_i=Z for every i, where Z is a nonconstant finite-variance nonnormal variable. Then S_n/n=Z for all n, so it does not converge in probability to E Z, and the standardized sums do not converge to N(0,1). Separately, constant X_i have sigma=0 and make the CLT normalization 0/0. The appendix must retain iid and 0<sigma^2<infinity (and finite E|X_1| for SLLN); its current shorthand is unsafe as a standalone formula reference.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_11_math finding L11-M-001 independently identifies the zero-variance defect; the iid omission is independently demonstrated here.

category: appendix correlation formulas omit their common positive-variance domain
dependency_chain: The appendix defines rho and states the |rho|=1 characterization at 246-247, then uses rho(X,X+Y) and rho(X_1,S_n) at 252-255. Lecture 7 defines rho only with a nonzero denominator and its correlation theorems/supplement rely on that domain.
independent_analysis: If X is constant, Var(X)=0 and rho(X,Y) is undefined, although every appendix line is written as unconditional. For independent iid constants, rho(X_1,S_n) is 0/0 rather than 1/sqrt(n). Where rho is defined, the equality characterization must read Y=aX+b almost surely, not pointwise. State 0<Var(X),Var(Y)<infinity; for the sum identities also require the indicated mutual independence and nondegenerate variance.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_07_math findings L07-M-004 and L07-M-005 validate the same domain issue; counterexamples above are independent.

category: appendix transformation recipes overstate the theorem carried from Lecture 8
dependency_chain: The appendix says a merely monotone g gives a density by the inverse-derivative formula (269-272), and gives the two-dimensional Jacobian recipe (280-296). Lecture 8 supplies the source one-dimensional theorem, while Lecture 9 uses a substantially stronger bijective/Jacobian setup for vectors.
independent_analysis: Even for g(x)=e^x and a standard-normal X, g^{-1}(y) is undefined for y<=0, so the stated formula cannot be a density on all real y without the omitted zero-outside-image clause. More generally strict monotonicity alone need not provide differentiability/absolute continuity sufficient to preserve a density. The recipe needs conditions such as an appropriate C^1 one-to-one map with nonzero derivative on the relevant support, an a.e. interpretation, and f_Y=0 off the image. Conditional-density division at 276-279 also needs f_X(x)>0 and is only defined a.e. These omissions make the appendix stronger than the usable theorem.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_08_math finding L08-M-006 and lecture_09_math finding F09-06 independently identify the regularity/support gaps.

category: appendix repeats an insufficient pivot condition as a construction rule
dependency_chain: The appendix claims that a central statistic monotone in theta with parameter-free distribution can be inverted into an interval (376-378). This imports the general construction from Lecture 13:32-37 and applies it as a formula rule.
independent_analysis: Weak monotonicity does not guarantee an inverse or finite endpoints. Take T(X,theta)=Z with Z~N(0,1) independent of theta: it is both nondecreasing and nonincreasing in theta and has a theta-free distribution, yet q_1<T<q_2 contains no information with which to bound theta. Require strict monotonicity together with solvability/range conditions, or specify a generalized-inverse construction and parameter-space constraints.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_13_math finding L13-M-002 independently supplied the same counterexample class.

category: one-sample and regression t inference are merged without their different sample/design prerequisites
dependency_chain: The appendix prints S^2 with denominator n-1 at 368-371 and the t(n-1) interval at 381-383 without conditions. Lecture 13 derives the one-sample result from iid normal observations. Lecture 14 then says its residual result works "as in Lecture 13" at 236-240 but uses chi-square(n-2), an RSS/(n-2) estimator, and t(n-2).
independent_analysis: S^2 is undefined at n=1; t(0) is not a Student law. Regression needs further conditions absent from the transfer: n>=3, a rank-two/nonconstant fixed design A=sum(X_k-Xbar)^2>0, sigma^2>0, and independent Gaussian errors. With n=2 and X_1!=X_2, OLS interpolates both observations so RSS/(n-2)=0/0. The appendix needs at least n>=2, sigma^2>0, and an iid-normal qualification for its one-sample formulas; the Lecture-14 bridge must not make the n-1 result look interchangeable with the n-2 regression result.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_13_math finding L13-M-005 and lecture_14_math findings F14-001 through F14-003 corroborate each prerequisite; the n=2 construction is independently supplied here.

category: appendix presents fixed-value conditional expectation as universally defined
dependency_chain: The appendix states E[X_1 | S_n=t]=t/n for independent iid variables at 256-257, then places it alongside standard conditional-expectation identities. Lecture 7 gives the same informal fixed-sum argument; Lecture 8's discrete construction defines conditioning through positive-probability atoms.
independent_analysis: For continuous iid variables such as exponentials, P(S_n=t)=0 for every fixed t, so elementary conditioning on that event is undefined. The robust statement is the a.s. identity E[X_1 | S_n]=S_n/n under integrability; a statement at each t needs a specified regular conditional version. Positive finite variances are also needed for adjacent correlation formulas, but are not enough to define conditioning at a null value.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_07_math finding L07-M-005 and lecture_08_math conditioning findings corroborate the atom/null-event distinction.

category: appendix repeats incorrect/incomplete discrete-distribution boundary conventions
dependency_chain: The discrete table and quick-reference block repeat Bin/Geo/NegBin/Poi formulas and state one mode at 154. Their source mode supplement is Lecture 6:267-278; the counting quantities feeding the table are developed in Lecture 15.
independent_analysis: The mode line is false at ties and a boundary: if m=(n+1)p is an integer with 0<p<1, Bin(n,p) has two modes m-1,m; p=1 makes floor(p(n+1))=n+1 outside the support. If lambda is a positive integer, Poi(lambda) has modes lambda-1,lambda. The table also needs its parameter domains, including 0<p<=1 for Geo/NegBin (p=0 does not define a finite waiting time), 0<=p<=1 for Bin/Ber, lambda>=0, and valid integer ranges for n,r,N,M. The appendix's standalone summary otherwise conflicts with the definitions it is meant to consolidate.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_06_math findings L06-M-005/L06-M-006 and lecture_15_math boundary findings corroborate these domain and tie cases.

category: continuous-distribution appendix table omits parameter/support domains
dependency_chain: The appendix's continuous table is used as the shared source for Normal, Exponential, Gamma, chi-square and t formulas. These laws supply the standardizations and pivots of Lectures 11, 13, and 14, but the table leaves their parameter domains implicit.
independent_analysis: The displayed densities/standardizations require a<b for U(a,b), lambda>0 for Exponential, alpha>0 and beta>0 (rate convention) for Gamma, sigma>0 for Normal, and positive integral degrees of freedom for chi-square/t in this course. Without sigma>0, the Normal density and (X-mu)/sigma are undefined; beta<=0 or alpha<=0 makes the stated Gamma expression nonnormalizable. Put the domains in the table headings or each row so downstream inference cannot invoke invalid parameter cases.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_09_math findings F09-03/F09-08 and lecture_11_math finding L11-M-010 corroborate the source-law restrictions.

category: proved theorem is narrower than stated, then is used later as the unrestricted prerequisite
dependency_chain: Lecture 11 states the finite-variance iid CLT at 19-25. Its proof adds "assume M_X1 is defined for all t" at 209, then uses an MGF Taylor expansion and MGF convergence at 215-225. Lecture 13:286-287 subsequently invokes the CLT for an arbitrary finite-mean/finite-variance X, and the appendix repeats the unrestricted CLT at 358-360.
independent_analysis: The MGF argument can prove only a narrower theorem. A centered, rescaled iid Student-t(3) sequence has finite positive variance and satisfies the stated CLT, but its MGF is infinite for every nonzero t, so it is excluded by line 209 and cannot enter the proof. In addition, Lecture 13 drops even the iid sampling condition when extending the claim: setting all X_i equal to one nonnormal finite-variance X defeats its conclusion at every n. Either label Lecture 11's argument as an MGF-neighborhood proof and use a characteristic-function proof for the stated CLT, or narrow every downstream statement consistently; Lecture 13 must add iid/appropriate CLT assumptions and remove the universal n>=30 guarantee.
review_corroboration: Completed lecture_11_math finding L11-M-005 and lecture_13_math finding L13-M-006 independently validate both links in this cross-lecture failure chain.
